summary: H.R. 6670, titled the "Temporary Family Visitation Act," establishes a new nonimmigrant visa category for certain relatives of United States citizens and lawful permanent residents seeking to visit the U.S. temporarily for family purposes. The bill sets specific rules for financial support, travel medical insurance, limits the length of stay to 90 days per calendar year, and restricts changes of status for individuals admitted under this new category.

affected_groups.effect: Can petition for eligible relatives to visit the United States temporarily for family purposes, provided they submit financial support declarations and meet compliance rules.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents

affected_groups.effect: May apply for a new temporary family purpose visa allowing stays of up to 90 days per calendar year, provided they meet insurance, financial, and departure-intent requirements.
affected_groups.group: Foreign Relatives of U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents

key_provisions: Creates a new nonimmigrant visa category (family purpose visa) under the Immigration and Nationality Act for relatives of U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents visiting for social, occasional, major life, religious, or other family events.
Defines eligible relatives to include spouses, children, sons, daughters, grandchildren, parents, grandparents, great-grandparents, siblings, uncles, aunts, nieces, and nephews.
Requires a financial support declaration, short-term travel medical insurance or international health insurance coverage for the stay, and a signed statement affirming intent to depart.
Limits the authorized period of admission to a maximum of 90 days per calendar year.

Disqualifies petitioners from sponsoring a relative if a previously sponsored relative under this category overstayed their authorized admission, subject to certification rules and criminal penalties for false statements.
Prohibits individuals admitted under this specific family purpose visa category from changing their status to another nonimmigrant class.
Allows individuals awaiting an immigrant visa to be eligible for a family purpose visa despite general presumptions of immigrant intent, with certain limitations.
